name: wired-target-example
notes: An example of a profile that also says how the rig reaches the system around a call. Copy it, keep the copy outside the repository if it names anything real, and replace every <PLACEHOLDER>. Each command is a list (a program, then each argument) and is run without a shell from the directory the batch is started in, so give paths that hold from there or absolute ones. Connection details are never written here: the read-back script takes them from SYNTHIQ_READBACK_DSN and SYNTHIQ_READBACK_SCOPE_ID. Check the whole thing with: synthiq-caller batch <scenarios> --target <this file> --leg fake --clips <bank> --out <dir> --dry-run. The commands below follow the product's fixture tooling: 'restore' puts the test tenant back to its seeded state, 'adopt' records what the call just created as the rig's own so that a later purge may remove it. allow_mutating is the most a batch may change here; it does not switch mutation on, the batch's --allow-mutating does.
